title: Transport an ordinary normalized Hom comparison to the one-point ring site
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings and φ:A→B. Let F and hF specify objects of scalar extension as in [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map], and M,N be module sheaves on the one-object bottom-topology site. Put M₀=M(*) and N₀=N(*), with B an A-algebra via φ. Given any B-linear map k:B tensor_A Hom_A(M₀,N₀)→Hom_B(B tensor_A M₀,B tensor_A N₀) with k(b tensor f)(c tensor x)=bc tensor f(x), there is a sheaf morphism g:F(Hom_A(M,N))→Hom_B(F(M),F(N)) satisfying the same identity using ringExtensionPure at every U; IsIso g if and only if k is bijective. No finiteness, projectivity or flatness is assumed.

proof.text: Evaluation at the unique object is an equivalence from sheaves of modules on the one-object bottom-topology site to modules. The inverse takes constant modules; every presheaf is a sheaf. The unique arrows between objects induce inverse restriction maps by the presheaf laws. The slice has the same property, so identity-slice evaluation identifies internal-Hom sections with ordinary linear maps. The inverse sends a linear map to its conjugates by the restriction isomorphisms; naturality proves both inverse identities.

The change-of-rings presheaf evaluates to B tensor_A M(*). Its sheafification unit is invertible (Presheaf.isSheaf_bot and CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify) and B-linear (the module sheafification unit). Composing its component with eqToHom(hF(M).symm) gives a B-linear equivalence sending b tensor x to ringExtensionPure. Apply this to M, N, and internal Hom.

Conjugate k by the source and target identifications from the preceding two steps. Full faithfulness of evaluation gives the sheaf map g. Evaluation reflects isomorphisms, and the conjugating maps are linear equivalences, hence IsIso g iff k is bijective. The pure-tensor identity at the unique object is hk under those identifications. Naturality of g, internal Hom, the unit and pure tensors restricts that identity to every U. This argument uses no projectivity or finiteness assumption.

theorem ringHomExtension_transport
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B)
    (F : RingSiteModules A ⥤ RingSiteModules B)
    (hF : ∀ M, F.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings (ringSiteMap φ) M)
    (M N : RingSiteModules A) :
    letI := φ.toAlgebra
    ∀ (k : B ⊗[A] ((M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)) →ₗ[A]
          (N.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))) →ₗ[B]
        ((B ⊗[A] (M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))) →ₗ[B]
          (B ⊗[A] (N.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)))))
      (hk : ∀ (b c : B)
        (f : M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) →ₗ[A] N.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))
        (x : M.val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)),
        k (b ⊗ₜ[A] f) (c ⊗ₜ[A] x) = (b * c) ⊗ₜ[A] f x),
    ∃ g : F.obj (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) M N) ⟶
        SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf B) (F.obj M) (F.obj N),
      (IsIso g ↔ Function.Bijective k) ∧ ∀ (U : (Discrete PUnit.{u + 1})ᵒᵖ) (b c : B)
        (f : (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) M N).val.obj U)
        (x : M.val.obj U),
        ((g.val.app U (ringExtensionPure φ F hF _ U b f)).app
          (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop)))) (ringExtensionPure φ F hF M U c x) =
        ringExtensionPure φ F hF N U (b * c) ((f.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U.unop)))) x)
